clue.text: Suits returned smelt, perhaps, quite starchy

indicators.note: returned means the word for suits is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: suits as a verb means fits, as clothes fit you
a smelt is a small fish, so this is a fish by example

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a returned batch of suits smelt and seemed rather heavily starched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns FITS into STIF; 'smelt' is the fish, not the past tense of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffish means somewhat stiff, and a starchy manner or fabric is stiff.

clue.text: Roman defence to set about English. he-man

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the letters of to are wrapped round the rest

parts.note: taken as written
a stud is a virile, macho man

explanation.surface: A Roman military manoeuvre is being turned against a burly Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: A testudo was the shield-roof formation; 'he-man' reads as a muscleman, but a stud is a virile man.
explanation.definitionFit: The testudo was the Roman tortoise formation of locked shields, a defensive tactic of the legions.

clue.text: Superwaif tucked into food, which exaggerated the hips

indicators.note: tucked into means one piece is placed inside the word for food

parts.note: fare is food, as in simple fare
a superwaif is a very skinny girl, split here as THIN GAL

explanation.surface: A stick-thin model tucks into a meal, while a garment flatters her hips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' places THIN GAL inside FARE; the definition is a description in clause form, as the garment is what did the exaggerating.
explanation.definitionFit: A farthingale was a hooped petticoat worn under skirts to widen them greatly at the hips.

clue.text: Drive that is restricting politician to D the left

indicators.note: restricting means holding something in, so the abbreviation for that is surrounds the politician

parts.note: i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for that is
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A motivating force keeps a politician from drifting leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'D' in the held text is an OCR slip and plays no part; 'that is' is the Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward, as a motive impels action.

clue.text: Savage woman overcome by passion

indicators.note: in a down clue, being overcome by something means sitting beneath it

parts.note: heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment
hen is a slang word for a woman

explanation.surface: A wild woman is swept away by strong emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by' puts HEN under HEAT in this down entry; 'Savage' is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen, in older usage, is an uncivilised person, the same sense as a savage.

clue.text: The crunch matter for slimmer is pace, having lost it

indicators.note: having lost means the word for pace drops some letters

parts.note: celerity means speed or swiftness

explanation.surface: A dieter's big decision is about speed, now that the momentum has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' takes IT out of CELERITY. 'The crunch' is not the decisive moment: it is the crunchiness of the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The crunchy stalks of this vegetable are a classic low-calorie food for dieters.

clue.text: Peach of a movie? It's a wrap!

parts.note: a cling, or clingstone, is a peach whose flesh sticks to the stone
a film is a movie

explanation.surface: A film director, delighted with the movie, declares shooting finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a wrap!' is the film-set cry at the end of shooting, but here it means a kitchen wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin plastic sheet is used to wrap and cover food.

clue.text: Madeleine's gathered flowers in Honolulu

indicators.note: gathered means the letters are collected from within the word Madeleine

explanation.surface: Madeleine picked a bunch of blossoms while in Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: Social order superior to new way of life

indicators.note: in a down clue, being superior means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: a regime is a system of government or social order

explanation.surface: A social system is claimed to be better than a new lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior to' places REGIME above N in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of living, such as a diet or exercise routine.

clue.text: Make just enough bread to butter a crust?

definitions.text: Make just enough bread to butter a crust?

parts.words: Make just enough bread to butter a crust?
parts.note: reads as spreading butter thinly on bread, but bread and crust are both slang for money and a livelihood, so it means earning barely enough

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is money and 'earning a crust' is making a living; to scrape butter is to spread it thinly.
explanation.definitionFit: To barely earn enough to live on is to get by with little money.

clue.text: Measure taken to curb the nightmare of public transport?

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain or cut short, so the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: a hellish journey by bus, BUS HELL

explanation.surface: Steps are taken to fix the horrors of commuting by public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to curb' trims the last L from BUS HELL; 'taken' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is a unit of dry volume, used for measuring grain and fruit.

clue.text: Excited, bound to be an event

parts.note: high means excited or elated
a bound is a jump or leap

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled is sure to make a big occasion of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain' (bound to be), but it is a noun meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: This leaping contest is an athletics field event.

clue.text: Bring up philosopher's dog

parts.note: to jack up is to raise or lift, as with a car
Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: Someone raises a famous thinker's pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' suggests rearing a pet, but it means raise with a jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jack Russell is a small terrier breed.

clue.text: Where divine law handed out, US nation wrong in a big way

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the big road

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's major motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of us nation are put into a different order

explanation.surface: An American nation goes badly astray where commandments were once given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes the anagram and 'in' the container. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; 'in a big way' sounds like 'enormously'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible says Moses received the Ten Commandments from God on this mountain.

clue.text: Hidden device — serious getting rush caught in areas where set up

clue.text: Pronouncement for murderer, punishment

indicators.note: a pronouncement is a spoken statement, so the word that follows is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer

explanation.surface: A judge hands down a sentence for a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronouncement' suggests a judge's sentence, but it signals that CAIN is to be said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane was a beating with a stick, long used as school punishment.

clue.text: Short girl, fantastic

indicators.note: short means the girl's name is cut by its final letter

parts.note: Megan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A petite girl is described as terrific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the girl's height, but it cuts the N from MEGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for tremendous or great.

clue.text: Top of encephalon acquired tear, producing swelling of head

indicators.note: top of means the first letter, which in a down entry is the top one

parts.note: got means acquired
a rip is a tear

explanation.surface: A brain injury leads to a swollen head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swelling of head' sounds medical, but means conceit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is self-indulgent behaviour that boosts one's vanity, a figurative big head.

clue.text: On river, securing room to manoeuvre, I'll perform this?

definitions.text: On river, securing room to manoeuvre, I'll perform this?

parts.note: the Esk is a river in northern England and Scotland

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the letters of I'll grip the shuffled word

parts.note: the letters of I'll, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: to manoeuvre means to shift around, so the letters of room are reordered

explanation.surface: A kayaker on a river, given space to move, promises to perform a certain move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to manoeuvre' makes the anagram and 'securing' the container. Read whole, a kayaker with room on the river would do this.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eskimo roll is the kayaking move of righting a capsized boat by rolling it upright.

clue.text: Potassium, given time, can form protein

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium
an era is a period of time
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Potassium, given enough time, may build up protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, but it is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratin is the fibrous protein that makes up hair, nails and horn.

clue.text: Boy pins cheque, but restriction put on Books Fi pin

clue.text: Man honoured to be given an ear to study — yellow

definitions.text: Man honoured to be given an ear

parts.note: to study is to read, as in reading law
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man is honoured to have someone listen while he studies a yellow book.
explanation.walkthrough: A successful bullfighter is awarded the bull's ear; 'given an ear' suggests being listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, who may be awarded an ear of the bull for a fine performance.

clue.text: Make stoop round ankles, ultimately

indicators.note: round means the word for stoop goes around the next letter

parts.note: to stoop is to deign, condescending to do something

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of ankles

explanation.surface: A person is told to bend down round their ankles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts DEIGN around S, the last letter of 'ankles'.
explanation.definitionFit: To design is to plan and make, as in designing a building.

clue.text: To prepare speech, Bill goes AWOL

indicators.note: goes AWOL means deserts, so the bill's letters leave the speech

parts.note: an address is a formal speech
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: To get his speech ready, a soldier named Bill deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a deserting soldier, but it is an advertisement, AD, removed from ADDRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress food is to prepare it, as with dressing a salad or a chicken.

clue.text: He has checked trousers, but there could be penny pocketed in the back

indicators.note: pocketed in means the jumbled letters are put inside the word for the back

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: could be means the letters of but there and the penny are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man wears check trousers, but there might be a penny in his back pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' makes the anagram and 'pocketed in' the container. The children's comic character wears yellow checked trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Bear, the British children's comic character, is famous for his yellow checked trousers and scarf.

clue.text: For pastry, cost evens out?

indicators.note: evens out means the even-placed letters of the word for cost are removed

parts.note: cost means price

explanation.surface: A cafe asks whether the cost of a pastry balances out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evens out' removes the second and fourth letters, R and C, of PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a dish baked in pastry.

clue.text: Look to retire on winning maintenance

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the previous piece

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: A retiree hopes to look after a win and keep their maintenance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' turns PEEK into KEEP, which goes on UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of maintaining something in good condition.

clue.text: Chick getting under duvet?

definitions.meaning: a young bird still in the nest
snuggling cosily down under the bedcovers

explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a baby bird not yet fledged, and nestling also means snuggling down.
